locations: Vörösmarty Square: | In the spring, this square becomes like a small “city within a city”. Flower bouquets, the smell of vanilla and cinnamon from the stalls, people walking around with ice cream, street musicians… Everything is bustling. If you like to observe life around you, this is the perfect place. The whole square looks like a mini festival, but in the most relaxed version.

St. Stephen's Basilica Square: | Spring has a special vibe here: warmth, blue skies, and a huge basilica casting a shadow like in an epic movie. At this time of year, the square is often filled with spring stalls selling crafts and trinkets — from scented soaps to small art prints. It's the perfect place to sit on a bench and enjoy a cake or a chocolate croissant.

Gozsdu Udvar – Easter Craft Market: | During the spring, Gozsdu turns into a true handmade paradise: miniature figures, film illustrations, handmade bracelets, decorative rabbits and colorful eggs, all handmade. In the evening hours (teen-friendly!) the lights are on, street music is playing and the atmosphere is just that — 'I have to paint this'.

ideas: Thermal bath night sessions: | In the summer, thermals are a real relief at night — cooler air, warm water, and a magical atmosphere under the pool lights.
Walks on Margaret Island: | In summer, the island is one big green haven: shade under the trees, birdsong, and a peaceful walk away from the city crowds.
Evening Danube cruise :| On hot days, an evening cruise is the perfect 'cool down' — breeze + illuminated bridges = a great sight.

Rooftop bars (non-alcoholic cocktails): | Summer evenings + panoramic views of the city + an ice-cold non-alcoholic cocktail = the perfect chill place to relax above the hustle and bustle of the city.
Gelato at Gelarto Rosa: | During the summer heat — an icy, pink gelato masterpiece. A cold, delicious and Instagrammable dessert for the end of the day.

City Park | Városliget morning walk |A gentle morning awakening in the most famous park in the city. Ducks, a pond, trees, a mini castle… everything has the perfect 'let's chill' energy. 🌿💛| Vajdahunyad Castle | This castle looks like you've stepped into a fantasy movie. Great for photos + a total architectural mix.

Museum visit | Museum of Fine Arts or Hall of Art: | Fine Arts Museum → classical art, pharaohs, renaissance. | Műcsarnok / Hall of Art → more modern, more creative, exhibitions that touch your brain and heart. 🎨💫
Thermal relaxation | Széchenyi Thermal Bath: the most famous thermal bath 🔥💦| Huge, yellow, warm, beautiful – everything a thermal bath should be.Teens-friendly: pools, mineral water, vacation 10/10.

Warm cafés | Gerbaud Café: classic, historic pastry shop (try the Esterházy or Dobos cake) | Book Café (Lotz Hall): a hidden gem, the ceiling looks like a mini opera.Perfect for tea + cookies + chill after a thermal bath.| Tea & cakes chill time

locations: 🎁 Vörösmarty Square – the heart of Christmas cheer: | During the holidays, the square turns into a real small winter town: wooden houses with handicrafts, the smell of warm cinnamon, bright lights on all sides and a big Christmas tree in the center. The atmosphere is lively, but also cozy — an ideal place to relax, look at the decorations and enjoy warm cakes.

Basilica Christmas Fair: | The square in front of the basilica looks like it fell out of a holiday movie: lightly snowing (if you're lucky), a huge illuminated facade, projections on the walls of the church and stalls that smell of sweets and hot drinks. Everything is very romantic, but also family-friendly and peaceful — perfect for an evening walk and photos that look like postcards.

places: Buda Castle district: | Old historical quarter full of narrow streets, museums, beautiful viewpoints and buildings from different periods. You can see the Royal Palace, the National Gallery, the old city walls and a panorama of all of Pest.

Matthias Church: | The church is known for its colorful, ceramic roof and detailed Gothic architecture. Inside, it's full of historical symbols, stained glass, and decorations — it looks like a small art treasure trove.

Fisherman's Bastion: | A fairytale terrace with towers and arches offering one of the most beautiful views of the Danube, the Parliament and the entire city. An ideal place for taking photos and enjoying the panorama.
what_to_get: 📜 Historical postcards: | These are postcards with old photos of Budapest — bridges, streets, trams, and buildings from the last century. They look like a little window into the city's past and are great as a small, lightweight souvenir that carries a story.

🏰 Miniature castle replicas:| Small models of Buda castles or famous buildings, made of metal or ceramic. They are great for shelves or a desk, because they look like you have your own little piece of Budapest at home.

places: 🎨 Hungarian National Gallery: | In this gallery you can see a huge collection of Hungarian art — from medieval icons and Renaissance paintings to modern artists. There are also beautiful panoramas from the castle terraces, so you can combine art + a beautiful view of the city.

🎭 Street-art areas in District VII (Erzsébetváros): | This area is known for its huge murals, creative graffiti and hidden art walls. Every passage or street has some cool drawing, and the whole atmosphere is young, urban and colorful — like a big open-air street-art museum.
what_to_get: 🖼️ Art prints: | These are art posters and printed illustrations made by local artists in a variety of styles — from minimalist drawings and retro posters of Budapest, to modern graphic works or fantasy scenes. They're lightweight, easy to carry, and look great as room decor.

🏺 Handmade ceramics: | Ručno pravljene šolje, tanjiri, činije i ukrasne figurice, često sa mađarskim motivima ili modernim dizajnom. Svaki komad je jedinstven, jer se oblikuje i oslikava ručno. Odlični su kao praktičan, ali i umetnički suvenir.

places: 🌿 Margaret Island: | A peaceful, green island in the middle of the Danube, full of tree-lined streets, walking paths, flower gardens and open grassy areas. You can see a mini zoo, a Japanese garden and beautiful fountains — the perfect place for a relaxing nature break away from the city bustle.

🌳 City Park (Városliget): | The largest city park in Budapest, surrounded by lakes, promenades and wide green spaces. It also houses Vajdahunyad Castle, a zoo and botanical areas, so you can combine nature, beautiful landscapes and a bit of leisurely exploration through the various parts of the park.
what_to_get: 🌱 Botanical postcards: | Postcards with illustrations of local plants, trees or flowers from Budapest's parks and gardens. They often look like little vintage botanical studies — delicate, detailed and great to keep as a keepsake.

📸 Nature photography prints: | High-quality photos of natural scenes from Margaret Island or City Park — flowers, lakes, avenues of trees, or animals from the area. They are ideal as room decor, as they carry a peaceful, natural energy.

places: 🎨 Simple Garden – a creative “labyrinth” full of energy: | Although it's known as a ruin bar, for visitors of your age, the most interesting part is the artistic-alternative atmosphere: colorful walls, unusual decorations, retro furniture, graphics, installations, and a constant lively crowd. The place seems like a huge creative chaos — but a fun one at that.

🌙 Gozsdu Udvar nightlife zone – lively street energy: | In the evening, Gozsdu Passage becomes a lit-up pedestrian zone full of people, lanterns, street musicians, and small handicraft shops. | For teenagers, it's great for: walking through the colorful arcades looking at art stalls grabbing street food (no alcohol) taking photos because of the really nice ambiance The whole atmosphere is lively, but you don't have to go to the bars — just walk around and soak up the energy.
what_to_get: 🎁 Budapest-themed souvenirs: | These are classic, but often creatively made souvenirs with Budapest motifs: mini magnets with bridges, illustrations of the Parliament, mugs with a panorama of the city, small tram models, stickers and retro postcards. They are ideal as light, practical mementos.

✨ Minimalist nightlife merch: | In Szimpli and Gozsd, you can sometimes find simple, modern souvenirs inspired by the city's nighttime atmosphere: black-and-white illustrations of alleys, stylized posters of lamps and alleys, small prints with geometric shapes, canvas bags or stickers with clean, minimalist designs. No party motifs — more of an 'urban vibe in a stylish version'.

places: 🍲 Paprika Vendéglő: | This restaurant is a classic representative of Hungarian local cuisine, so you can find: * Goulash soup (rich, spicy but not too hot) * Pörkölt (something like Hungarian stew with pasta)Csirkepaprikás (chicken stew with dumplings) * Lángos (fried dough with sour cream and cheese) * Drum cake or Esterházy cake for dessert | Everything is warm, homemade and super delicious.

🛒 Great Market Hall (Nagy Vásárcsarnok): | This is a huge indoor market, so you can try and buy a bunch of local specialties there: * Lángos (the most famous street food in Budapest) * Hortobágyi palacsinta (savory pancakes filled with meat or vegetables) * Kolbász (local sausage — you can choose milder varieties) * Sarma / stuffed cabbage (Hungarian style) * Roasted peppers and spicy spreads * Hungarian sweets: strudel (strudel), honey cake (medenjaci)
what_to_get: 🌶️ Hungarian paprika – a symbol of Hungarian cuisine: | Hungarian paprika is special because it has an intense aroma, but it doesn't have to be spicy — it's often sweet or slightly smoky. It's dried and ground in the traditional way, giving that distinctive flavor to Hungarian dishes like goulash and paprikash. | It's one of the most authentic ingredients you can take home.

🥐 Local pastries – soft, rich and super fragrant: | Hungarian pastries are known for their layered dough, nuts, vanilla, and mild sweetness. Specialties like Dobos cake, Esterházy cake, or various rétes (strudels) are a blend of traditional recipes and beautiful, rich flavors. | Each dessert has a bit of a “homemade” energy — like eating pastries from an old European pastry shop.

places: 🔥💦 Széchenyi Thermal Bath – the most famous thermal bath: | Huge, yellow, warm, beautiful – everything a thermal suit should be. | Teens-friendly: swimming pools, mineral water, vacation 10/10.

💦 Gellért Bath – „kupanje u umetničkom delu“: | This thermal bath feels like you’ve entered a vast Art Nouveau palace: colorful mosaic tiles, stained glass windows, columns, and elegant pools. The experience is a combination of relaxing in the warm water and the feeling of being in a historic spa. | The atmosphere is peaceful, beautiful, and completely different from modern pools — it’s like you’re on a “retro spa trip” in the heart of Budapest.
what_to_get: 🧴 Spa products: | In thermal baths, you can find a variety of creams, gels, and oils inspired by local mineral springs. They usually have mild, natural scents and packaging with bath motifs. They are designed to relax your skin after a bath — small, practical “spa souvenirs” that you can easily take home.

🧂 Thermal salts: | These are sachets or jars of salt enriched with minerals from Hungarian thermal waters. When added to the bath, they slowly melt and give the warm water a calming, spa-like feel. They are a popular souvenir because they bring some of the spa atmosphere to your home.

Relaxed, nice for taking photos, and the Danube always has that 'mini adventure' feeling.

ideas: 🎨 Outdoor Craft Markets: | Total charm! These are small, colorful markets full of handicrafts, local artists, jewelry, ceramics, soaps, decorations and trinkets that smell like “handmade”. Ideal for leisurely sightseeing, talking to craftsmen and finding something that is truly local, not mass-touristy. The whole atmosphere is great for walking and taking photos.

🌿 Riverside Walks: | A peaceful, relaxed and super pleasant experience. A walk along the Danube in Szentendre is gentle on the brain: the water is flowing, people are sitting on benches, everything is slow and uncrowded. Perfect for resetting, blazing, thinking or just enjoying the silence and nature.

⛴️ Danube Boat Ride: | You glide gently on the Danube in a boat while looking at the Szentendre waterfront, the forests and the small docks. Everything smells like summer, the water gently ripples and gives you the feeling of a mini-adventure without any effort. The best experience is in the afternoon or early evening, when the light is golden and chill.

🍦 Ice Cream Shops: | Sant'Andrea (Szentendre) in summer = ice cream is a must. In the old town there are several small gelaterias and local pastry shops with a huge selection of flavors — from classic chocolate to crazy fruit combinations. Grab a cone and stroll through the alleys like a true tourist on a mission for happiness.

🌆 Old Town Evening Walks: | Kad sunce padne, barokne ulice dobiju mekano, toplo svetlo i sve izgleda bajkovitije. Manje je gužve, vazduh se rashladi, a trgovi i prolazi postanu super romantični — ne romantični ka drugoj osobi, nego romantični ka životu 😄. Idealno za laganu šetnju, fotke i cool letnju atmosferu.

🍁 Skanzen Fall Festivals: | In autumn, the Skanzen turns into a total festival of atmosphere: the scents of roasted chestnuts, traditional food, handicrafts, live music and displays of ancient customs. Everything is colorful, full of leaves, a little rustic — as if you are in some old village celebrating autumn in the most beautiful way possible. Ideal for walking, enjoying and discovering how people once lived, prepared winter food and celebrated the season.

📷 Old Town Photography: | Autumn in the old town gives you the perfect mix of colors: baroque facades + orange leaves + soft autumn light = photogenic at its best. The alleys are quieter than in summer, the tones are warmer and everything looks like a small painting scene. Ideal for leisurely wandering, capturing details and taking photos that automatically look “artsy”.

locations: 🎄 Main Square Seasonal Christmas Fair: | The winter main square in Szentendre is like a small live Christmas movie: colorful houses, the smells of boiled juice, gingerbread and pastries, handicrafts made by local craftsmen and warm lights that turn everything into a cozy fairy tale. Music, ornaments, small workshops and decorations give a real holiday “hug” vibe. Ideal for walking, buying small gifts and enjoying that special winter mix of cold air + warm ambiance.

places: 🖼️ Serbian Orthodox Museum: | For those who love history, this is a real little gem: a collection of icons, old liturgical objects and artifacts that tell the story of the Serbian community in Szentendre through the centuries. It gives a great insight into the cultural life, migrations and traditions that shaped the city.

🏘️ Baroque Old Town: | The old town is like an open historical book: Baroque facades, squares and alleys dating back to the 18th century, when different communities mixed in Szentendre — Serbian, German, Hungarian. A walk through this part of the city gives a sense of a time when Szentendre was a bustling trading center full of artisans and travelers.
what_to_get: 🏺 Historical Replicas : | These are small objects modeled after old artifacts: mini icons, traditional ornaments, replicas of ancient tools or decorations. They are not just “pretty objects”, but also bring a sense of local history and culture. They are perfect for those who like to bring a piece of the past home — like keeping a small part of the museum on a shelf.

📮 Traditional Postcards: | Classic postcards with baroque streets, churches, the Danube and the bright colors of Szentendre. Simple, nostalgic and great to send or keep as a reminder of the city's atmosphere. They carry that warm 'I traveled here and it was wonderful' vibe.

places: 🎨 Art Mill Gallery: | A place for artistic souls: a modern gallery housed in an old mill, where traditional architecture merges with contemporary exhibitions. Inside, you can see works by local and regional artists, from paintings to installations. The entire space exudes creative energy and acts as a small cultural epicenter of Szentendre.

🍬 Marzipan Museum: | Za umetnike sa slatkim zubom — totalni vizualni spektakl. Figure, skulpture i minijaturne scene napravljene od marcipana izgledaju kao da ih je neko isklesao od šećera i mašte. Kombinuje zanat, humor i detaljnu izradu, pa deluje više kao galerija od slatkiša nego muzej.

🧶 Local Craft Shops: | Mala carstva rukotvorina gde svaki predmet ima dušu. Ručno rađena keramika, tkanine, drangulije, minijature, ilustracije i unikatni ukrasi — sve delo lokalnih umetnika i zanatlija. Sjajno za inspiraciju i za otkrivanje kako tradicionalni motivi žive u savremenom dizajnu.
what_to_get: 🏺 Handmade Ceramics: | Unique pots, cups, bowls and decorative pieces made by local craftsmen. Each item has its own character — the uneven glaze, the hand-drawn motifs, the warmth of the material. You take home a real little piece of Szentendre that is both practical and artistic.

🎨 Small Art Paintings: | Small paintings by local artists, mostly landscapes of the old town, the Danube or charming alleys. Each one is original and captures a moment that you can't take with you with any other souvenir. Ideal for a wall, table or shelf — as a daily little dose of inspiration.

places: 🌊 Danube Riverside: | The Danube Riverbank in Szentendre is a haven for nature lovers: calm water, shady trees, wide walking paths and riverside seating. Ideal for relaxing, bird watching, a light picnic or simply enjoying the ever-changing hues of the water.

🏡 Skanzen Outdoor Spaces: | The Skansen is like a large natural playground — wide fields, old farmhouses among the greenery, orchards, gardens, and country paths leading through open spaces. Here you can feel the silence, the smell of grass and trees, and walk through landscapes that seem to have been preserved from another time.
what_to_get: 📸 Nature Photography: | The most beautiful memory you can 'take home' from nature without any damage — just snap a photo and save the moment. Whether it's shots of the Danube, autumn colors, sun reflections, or details like leaves and pebbles, each photo becomes a small natural trophy that you take home only in your phone.

🖼️ Landscape Postcards: | If you want something you can hold in your hand, landscape postcards are perfect: the Danube at sunset, village scenes from the Skanzen, baroque streets with trees. You buy them in stores, and the resulting images always have that peaceful, natural vibe. They are great as a gift or to keep in a memory album.

places: 🧶 Local Craft Shops: | The Little Treasures of Szentendre — shops full of handicrafts made by local artisans. Here you can find handmade ceramics, fabrics, wooden decorations, unique jewelry and all those beautiful little things that have a “soul”. Each item is a small work of art and a great souvenir from the city.

🎨 Old-Town Ateliers: | Ateliers hidden in old baroque alleys — places where you can peek directly into the world of local artists. They are often small, quiet workshops with canvases, sketches and crafts in progress. Ideal for creative lovers who want to see art “in process”, not just in a shop window.
what_to_get: 🪵 Handmade Wooden Toys: | Cute, handmade wooden toys that exude nostalgia. Often painted in vibrant colors or left in their natural wood, each piece has that “warm, homey” feel. They are souvenirs that last, smell lovely like wood, and are reminiscent of traditional craftsmanship.

🎨 Folk-Art Items: | Objects inspired by folk art — embroideries, decorative boxes, textile patterns, miniature ornaments and motifs that originate from local traditions. These souvenirs carry the spirit of the region, its colors and symbols, and act as small pieces of cultural heritage that you can take home.

places: 🍽️ Local Restaurants: | Places where you can try real local food: goulash, stew, homemade soups, fish specialties along the Danube and traditional cakes. The ambiance is usually warm and homely, and the portions generous — ideal for anyone who likes to explore culture through a plate. Expect scents, spices and that old-fashioned cuisine that gives Sentandreja its special flavor.

☕ Old-Town Cafés: | Cafés located in the charming baroque streets of the old town. Inside — the smell of coffee, cakes and old wooden interiors; outside — small terraces with a view of the colorful facades. They are perfect for a break during a walk, a cake, hot chocolate or lemonade, and for sitting while watching the slow rhythm of Szentendre.
what_to_get: 🍬 Traditional Sweets: | Sweets that smell of tradition: handmade candies, marzipan figures, gingerbread, vintage cakes and local chocolate treats. Easy to carry, nicely packaged and great as a gift or a little “travel souvenir” when you return home.

🧀 Local Gourmet Products: | Real gastronomic souvenirs: homemade jams, spice mixes, honey, cheeses, and even local spreads or specialties in jars. Everything is full of authentic taste and comes from small, local productions. An ideal choice for food lovers who want to take a piece of Sant'Andrea in their backpack.

tour_type.morning: 🏰 Kalemegdan Fortress: * Starting at the most legendary place in the city — the fortress overlooking the confluence of the Sava and Danube. A little history, a little walking, a lot of beautiful views. → | 🗽 Victor Monument: * A Belgrade icon! It stands tall and overlooks the entire city. The panoramas from here are particularly strong — ideal for a “here I am above Belgrade” photo. → | 🎖️ Military Museum: * A museum with clear displays of military uniforms, objects and history through different eras. Everything is nicely arranged and gives a nice overview of the past. → | 🚶‍♂️ Walk Through Knez Mihailova Street: * The most famous pedestrian street — full of shops, street artists, old architecture and the hustle and bustle of the city. A classic Belgrade “must”. → | ☕ Coffee at Republic Square: End of the tour with a break at Republic Square: cafes, the Old Palace, the National Theater... an ideal place to rest and observe the city atmosphere.
tour_type.afternoon: 🍷 Skadarlija Bohemian Quarter: * You start in Belgrade's most charming street - cobblestones, old lanterns, murals, artists, live music (quiet in the morning, livelier in the evening). Shkadarlija always smells of tradition, history and the bohemian spirit of the city. → | 🍽️ Lunch with Serbian Specialties: * A real local feast awaits you here: ćevapi, sarma, gibanica, prebranac, ajvar... everything that Belgrade proudly serves. The ambiance is top-notch — rustic, cozy, and full of homely charm. → | ⚡ Nikola Tesla Museum: * After lunch — scientific magic. Interactive displays, Tesla's original objects and a great explanation of his brilliant life. Super interesting and very accessible, even if you are not a 'science nerd'. → |⛪ St. Sava Temple: * Finally, one of the largest Orthodox churches in the world. Imposing on the outside, peaceful and magnificent on the inside. The spacious courtyard and wide plateau are ideal for a leisurely stroll and the end of the tour.
tour_type.sunset: 🗼 Zemun Gardoš Tower Walk with Danube Views: * A walk to Gardoš is like a little escape from the center into a romantic, “old Zemun” vibe. Narrow cobblestone streets lead you to the famous tower from which you can enjoy a view of the Danube, boats, the quay and the whole of Zemun. A light wind blows up there, and the panorama looks like a perfect mix of history and nature. Ideal for photos, a leisurely walk and relaxation by the river.
tour_type.night: Savamala & Beton Hala cafés/bars (non-alcoholic options available) * Trendy riverfront spots with modern cafés and stylish lounges, perfect for relaxing by the water. The area mixes creative design, cool interiors, and great views of the Sava River. While some venues operate as bars with age restrictions, many offer plenty of non-alcoholic options like fresh juices, lemonades, iced teas, smoothies, and good coffee. Great for hanging out, people-watching, and enjoying the contemporary side of Belgrade’s vibe.

While some venues operate as bars with age restrictions, many offer plenty of non-alcoholic options like fresh juices, lemonades, iced teas, smoothies, and good coffee. ideas: 🌊 Riverside Walks (Dorćol & Zemun): * Spring + river = perfect combination. | In Dorćol, you can enjoy a peaceful walk along the Danube, bike paths and cafes with deck chairs. 🏖️ Ada Ciganlija Beach Day: | Belgrade’s “city seaside”! You can swim, rent a paddleboard, bike around the lake, or just chill on the shore. Lots of shade, snack spots, and a full-on summer vibe without leaving the city.

🌅 Danube & Sava Evening Walks: | When the heat finally calms down, the riverbanks come alive. Cool breezes, long paths for walking, great sunset views, and a super relaxed atmosphere. Perfect for unwinding after a hot day.

🍦 Gelato in the City Center: | Grab an ice cream in Knez Mihailova or around Republic Square and enjoy a sweet break while wandering through the historic streets. Summer survival kit = gelato + shade + slow stroll.

locations: ✨ Knez Mihailova Street Winter Market: | A festive stretch of wooden booths, lights, and holiday decorations along Belgrade’s main pedestrian street. You’ll find handmade ornaments, warm snacks, crafts, and that cheerful winter atmosphere that makes the whole street glow.

🎄 Republic Square Holiday Stalls: | The central square turns into a cozy holiday corner with small stalls offering gifts, seasonal treats, and local crafts. Bright lights, music, and a lively winter vibe make it a perfect stop during a holiday stroll.

places: 🏰 Kalemegdan Fortress: | A centuries-old fortress overlooking the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers. It combines ancient walls, old gates, scenic viewpoints, and layers of history from Romans, Ottomans, Austro-Hungarians, and more. A perfect open-air time-travel spot.

🏛️ National Museum: | Belgrade’s main museum, home to archaeology, medieval art, and modern history exhibits. You’ll find everything from ancient artifacts to famous paintings, giving a full overview of Serbia’s cultural and historical development in one place.

They’re great souvenirs for anyone who wants to bring home a little piece of history in a decorative, meaningful form.

🏛️ Museum-Themed Souvenirs: | Fun and educational keepsakes connected to Belgrade’s museums: postcards, notebooks, magnets, bookmarks, and items featuring famous exhibits or artworks. They’re perfect for history and culture fans who want something that reminds them of their museum visit.

places: 🖼️ Contemporary Art Museum (Ušće): | A bright, modern space showcasing Serbian and regional contemporary art — paintings, installations, multimedia works, and experimental pieces. 🧷 Indie Art Souvenirs: | Small, original items made by independent creators: stickers, mini-prints, badges, handmade notebooks, or tiny sculptures. Each piece reflects the artist’s own style, making these souvenirs fun, expressive, and totally unique compared to typical tourist items.

places: 🎧 Record Stores in Vračar: | Vračar has several cozy record shops where you can browse through vinyls, CDs, posters, and music merch. Great for discovering local bands, classic rock, jazz, and indie finds. The vibe is friendly and creative — perfect for anyone who loves digging through music history.

🎭 Savamala Cultural Bars (non-alcoholic options available): | Savamala has artsy, music-focused venues where you’ll find live performances, DJ sets, exhibitions, and creative events. 🎺 Street Musicians Around Knez Mihailova: | Knez Mihailova’s pedestrian zone is full of musicians — guitarists, violinists, sax players, small bands, and performers from different genres. It creates a lively, street-festival feel and adds a musical backdrop to your walk through the city center.

Even if you don’t have a record player yet, they make awesome décor and memories.
